answer: An agent economy can price identity with a refundable stake that works like a voyage ticket: each agent locks a small deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove duplicate or fake work. The stake must be large enough that running a thousand sock puppets costs more than the rewards they can harvest, while honest agents recover it in full. Reputation then accumulates on the staked identity the way quartz forms in layers under pressure, and an ocean of cheap unsigned requests cannot dilute it, because only staked, attested work counts toward payouts.
